svg.title: PostgreSQL entity-relationship diagram, derived from the migrations
svg.desc: All 41 tables of the mcp_saas schema grouped into five areas, with primary keys, declared foreign keys and columns.
svg.text: PostgreSQL ERD — derived from the migrations
Schema after all 49 migration files · 41 tables · physical schema: mcp_saas
Built by applying every migration, in order, to an empty PostgreSQL database and reading the result back from the catalog.

• Each table card shows its primary key (PK), its declared foreign keys (FK, with the target table and columns) and its other columns.
• Only declared relational keys are drawn as FK. Tenant, cluster, pattern and catalog-namespace identifiers are logical scope and are not enforced as physical foreign keys.
• Generic namespaced values (dimensions, attributes, relationships) are stored as identifiers and JSONB, so a new program or rule set adds rows, not tables.
• Eligibility criteria are held in the rule set tables: rule sets are keyed by content hash, and a separate head table points each program at its active rule set.
• Policy decisions and events reference exact manifest digests, and program-candidate decisions reference exact candidate digests.
Source of truth: db/migrations/ (types, constraints, indexes and exact SQL). This image shows the schema the migrations produce; it is not an introspection of a running database.
